title: EPFL BindCraft: One-Shot Open-Source Design of Functional Protein Binders via AlphaFold2 Backpropagation
whyItMatters: Published in Nature, EPFL’s open-source BindCraft backpropagated directly through AlphaFold2 to achieve 10–100% wet-lab hit rates across 12 diverse targets (including CRISPR-Cas9 and allergens), democratizing one-shot protein design.
summary: Published in Nature on August 27, 2025 (Vol. 646, pp. 483–492, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-025-09429-6), Martin Pacesa, Lennart Nickel, Bruno E. Correia, and collaborators at EPFL introduced BindCraft, an automated open-source pipeline that designs functional de novo protein binders in a single shot by backpropagating structural interface losses directly through AlphaFold2 weights, followed by ProteinMPNN sequence refinement and PyRosetta filtering. Across 12 diverse and challenging biological targets—including cell-surface receptors, allergens, de novo multi-domain proteins, and CRISPR-Cas9—BindCraft achieved 10% to 100% experimental success rates (averaging 46.3%) while testing only dozens of candidates per target, without requiring high-throughput screening facilities.
technicalHighlights: Backpropagates directly through AlphaFold2 to hallucinate complementary binding interfaces and sequences in one unified open-source workflow.
Achieved 10–100% experimental success rates (46.3% average) across 12 diverse targets, including functional inhibition of CRISPR-Cas9 and allergen neutralization.
Enabled ordinary academic wet labs without robotic display facilities to design nanomolar binders on standard GPUs.
caveats: Relies on AlphaFold2’s folded-protein structural priors, making highly disordered targets and small-molecule/covalent modalities harder without complementary all-atom tools.

scoreRationale.foundational: Showed that direct gradient backpropagation through AlphaFold2 achieves remarkably high zero-shot binder hit rates without training a new diffusion generator.
scoreRationale.ripple: Immediately became one of the most widely adopted open-source binder design tools worldwide, from gene-therapy AAV targeting to academic therapeutics.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (Vol. 646, pp. 483–492) with extensive wet-lab affinity, functional inhibition, and structural validation across 12 targets.
scoreRationale.velocity: Turned binder discovery from screening tens of thousands of yeast-display clones into testing a handful of one-shot designs.
